messages.subject: treatment comparisons within distance
parts:
I'm looking for the best way to analyze survey data comparing various =
protocols.
We have conducted an experimental seabird survey with two observers; =
where one was the reference using one protocol all along while the other =
was switching among three protocols to be tested against the reference. =
Since the three protocols were used in blocks (1-hour blocks, 20 min. =
per protocol within a block), I also need to take this random effect =
into account. We did not use capture-recapture because it would be =
impossible to ascertain which bird (or group) was detected or not by the =
two observers.

I'm more from a frequentist background, and modeling this analysis into =
a general linear model and contrast each treatment against the reference =
would be fairly straightforward using a stat package. However, I would =
like to take into account the detection rate, but at the same time I'm =
not looking for the most accurate density and just comparing apparent =
density might be ok too...I wonder however about how all this would =
affect variance estimates, as precision would be one way to judge the =
results.

On top of my head, I see several options:
1- somehow find a way to model all this correctly into Distance;
2- compute the detection function in Distance, somehow apply it to the =
data and analyze the results through a general linear model;
3- run a general linear model using the raw data;
4- others?

Any advice/idea welcome!


Fran=E7ois Bolduc
